samples.summary: editor.ts `siblingsOf` resolves cell parentage from the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`, so indent/outdent silently no-ops for a list item inside a header/footer table cell
samples.evidence: `forEachBlockInSelection`'s cursor-only fallback (editor.ts:1711) reads `layout.blockParentMap`, which is the BODY layout's map (`layout` is assigned only from `computeLayout(doc.document.blocks, …)` at editor.ts:1523; header/footer cell parentage lives in `headerLayout`/`footerLayout` and is merged only into `doc.setBlockParentMap` at editor.ts:1573-1580 — the comment at editor.ts:3350 documents exactly this body-only limitation). For a caret in a header/footer table cell, `cellInfo` is therefore `undefined`, so `siblingsOf` returns `doc.getContextBlocks()` (the header's TOP-LEVEL blocks). The cell block's id is not in that array, so `planSiblingGroup` never matches it and `planListLevelChanges` returns an empty plan — `editor.indent()`/`outdent()` change no list level at all. Before this change the fallback called `fn(block)` and the level was written by id, so the gesture worked. `text-editor.ts`'s `siblingsOf` avoids this by using `getActiveLayout()` via `getCellInfo` (text-editor.ts:3650); editor.ts should use the merged `doc.blockParentMap` instead.

samples.summary: Carrying children turns one indent gesture into N separate store writes without `Doc.batch()`, so under YorkieDocStore each carried child is its own undo/CRDT unit and Cmd+Z leaves the subtree half-moved
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` loops `doc.setBlockType(...)` once per planned block (editor.ts:1600-1611; identical loops in text-editor.ts:2717-2722 and text-box-editor.ts:826-831). `Doc.setBlockType` issues one `store.setBlockType` + `refresh()` per call, and `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` opens its own `withUpdate` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1535) — i.e. one Yorkie change and one `doc.history` entry per block, since only `batch()` collapses writes into a single undo unit (yorkie-doc-store.ts:567-574). `Doc.batch()` exists (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:146) and is not used here. Previously a single-caret indent was exactly one write; now a parent with k children is k+1 undo steps, and each intermediate undo state is precisely the parent-at-child-level corruption this PR exists to prevent (the same failure mode called out in document.ts:407-419 for Backspace). Remote peers also observe the intermediate states.

samples.summary: Outdenting a selection whose first item is already at level 0 is now a complete no-op for the entire selection, including deeper nested items the user explicitly selected
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` adds every subtree member to `covered` BEFORE the boundary checks (list-level.ts:70), then `continue`s on `delta < 0 && level <= 0` (line 73). So for a fully-selected list `a(0), b(1), c(2)`, `a`'s subtree covers `b` and `c`, `a` is refused, and `b`/`c` are skipped as covered — nothing moves. The old per-item code moved `b`→0 and `c`→1. Selecting a whole multi-level list and pressing Shift+Tab (a common flatten gesture, and what Google Docs does move) now produces no feedback at all. The behaviour is deliberate (pinned by the 'floor' test in test/model/list-level.test.ts), so this is flagged as a possibly-unintended product consequence rather than a coding slip.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf` calls `doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)`, which throws when the parent map is stale, turning an indent gesture into an uncaught exception
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1623 (and text-editor.ts:2877) resolve the table via `doc.getBlock(...)`, which throws `Block not found: …` (document.ts:215) rather than returning undefined. `blockParentMap` is only rebuilt at layout time (see document.ts:238-241 comment about entries predating the current document), so between deleting/replacing a table and the next layout, a lingering `cellInfo` makes indent/outdent throw where the old code — which only used `cellInfo` for `markDirty` — could not. `findBlock` (non-throwing) would be the safe read here.

samples.summary: Carried children are rewritten through `setBlockType` with `listKind` read off the child, so a child list-item with no `listKind` is silently coerced to 'unordered'
samples.evidence: The plan feeds `change.block.listKind` into `setBlockType(id, 'list-item', {listKind, listLevel})` (editor.ts:1601-1604 etc.), and both stores default a missing `listKind` to `'unordered'` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:337, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1506). Previously only blocks the user selected went through that path; now every carried child does, so any list-item whose `listKind` is absent (imported/CRDT-parsed data — crdt-tree.ts:243 only assigns when the attribute is present) has its kind rewritten as a side effect of indenting its parent.

mergedFrom.summary: `siblingsOf` calls `doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)`, which throws when the parent map is stale, turning an indent gesture into an uncaught exception
mergedFrom.evidence: editor.ts:1623 (and text-editor.ts:2877) resolve the table via `doc.getBlock(...)`, which throws `Block not found: …` (document.ts:215) rather than returning undefined. `blockParentMap` is only rebuilt at layout time (see document.ts:238-241 comment about entries predating the current document), so between deleting/replacing a table and the next layout, a lingering `cellInfo` makes indent/outdent throw where the old code — which only used `cellInfo` for `markDirty` — could not. `findBlock` (non-throwing) would be the safe read here.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `layout` in editor.ts is built solely from `computeLayout(doc.document.blocks, …)` (editor.ts:1523-1533); header/footer cell parentage lives in headerLayout/footerLayout and is merged only into `doc.setBlockParentMap` (editor.ts:1573-1580), a limitation the file itself documents at editor.ts:3346-3355. The cursor-only fallback at editor.ts:1711 reads the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`, so a caret inside a header/footer table cell yields `cellInfo === undefined`; `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1618-1627) then returns `doc.getContextBlocks()`, which for header context is the header's TOP-LEVEL block array (model/document.ts:158-162) and does not contain the cell block. `planListLevelChanges`/`planSiblingGroup` (model/list-level.ts:104-112, 57-67) only emit changes for ids found within the given sibling array, so the plan is empty and `applyListLevelChanges` (editor.ts:1595-1612) writes nothing; `indent()`/`outdent()` (editor.ts:3574-3604) skip list-items in their marginLeft branch, making the gesture a total no-op. No guard prevents this: header edit context is entered by real interaction (text-editor.ts:1920,1925), header/footer tables are a supported/handled shape (editor.ts:436-438; text-editor.ts:5043-5045), and the toolbar calls api.indent/outdent unconditionally (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949,953). The earlier selection branches do not rescue it — editor.ts:1665-1666 use the same body map and editor.ts:1684-1686 getBlockIndex returns -1 for cell blocks, funnelling back to the same fallback. The sibling implementation in text-editor.ts:2870-2880 correctly uses region-aware `getCellInfo`/`getActiveLayout` (text-editor.ts:3650-3655, 4591-4592), confirming editor.ts's variant is the defective one. Correctness lane (wrong data source → silently wrong/no result on a reachable path); major.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described. applyListLevelChanges (editor.ts:1595-1612, text-editor.ts:2712-2723, text-box-editor.ts:821) loops doc.setBlockType once per planned block with no batch. Doc.setBlockType (document.ts:653-668) does one store write + refresh per call; YorkieDocStore.setBlockType (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1489,1535) routes through withUpdate (:2866-2874) which opens a standalone doc.update when no batch is open, so each block is its own Yorkie change and its own doc.history entry — batch() (:2876-2916) is the only mechanism that collapses writes, and snapshot() (:2918-2921) is a no-op. Doc.batch() exists (document.ts:146-153) and is used elsewhere (editor.ts:1239, link-run.ts:101) but not by any caller of applyListLevelChanges (editor.ts:3574-3604, text-editor.ts:2701-2704/2750-2778, text-box-editor.ts:1163/1178) — I enumerated them and none is enclosed in a batch. The store is the production one (docs-view.tsx:356 constructs YorkieDocStore), so a single Tab/indent on a parent with k children produces k+1 undo units; one Cmd+Z reverts only the last carried child, leaving the subtree at mixed levels — the very inconsistency this path exists to preserve, and the same granularity hazard already documented at document.ts:404-419. Inconsistent state / broken invariant on a normal-use path is in the correctness lane; not refutable.

finding.summary: Outdenting a selection whose first item is already at level 0 is now a complete no-op for the entire selection, including deeper nested items the user explicitly selected
finding.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` adds every subtree member to `covered` BEFORE the boundary checks (list-level.ts:70), then `continue`s on `delta < 0 && level <= 0` (line 73). So for a fully-selected list `a(0), b(1), c(2)`, `a`'s subtree covers `b` and `c`, `a` is refused, and `b`/`c` are skipped as covered — nothing moves. The old per-item code moved `b`→0 and `c`→1. Selecting a whole multi-level list and pressing Shift+Tab (a common flatten gesture, and what Google Docs does move) now produces no feedback at all. The behaviour is deliberate (pinned by the 'floor' test in test/model/list-level.test.ts), so this is flagged as a possibly-unintended product consequence rather than a coding slip.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real and I reproduced it by reading the code: list-level.ts:69-70 adds the whole subtree to `covered` before the boundary checks, and list-level.ts:73 refuses a level-0 root, so a fully-selected nested list whose root is at level 0 yields an empty plan and nothing moves. But it is not a blocking correctness defect. (a) It is the module's documented contract, stated verbatim at list-level.ts:50-55 ("Boundaries apply to the subtree as a unit: outdent is refused when the root is already at level 0... A selected block already covered by an earlier item's subtree - refused or not - is skipped"), and pinned by test/model/list-level.test.ts:79-85. (b) The invariant the module exists to enforce (subtree relative depth survives the gesture, #1050) is upheld, not broken: moving b to 0 while a stays at 0 would flatten a child into a sibling of its own parent, the exact bug this code prevents. (c) No correctness cost when it fires - the consumer at editor.ts:1595-1612 iterates an empty change array, so no writes, no data loss, no partial/inconsistent state, no crash. (d) The logic is internally consistent with the ceiling path (test:99-101 shows only the offending subtree is refused); the whole-selection no-op arises solely because a fully-selected list is one subtree. Whether outdent should flatten (Google Docs style) or refuse as a unit is a product/UX semantics decision - the reviewer concedes "the behaviour is deliberate... a possibly-unintended product consequence rather than a coding slip" - which falls outside the Correctness lane (no wrong condition, off-by-one, inverted logic, missing guard, async mistake, leak, or broken invariant).

finding.summary: TextEditor selection walk still indexes body blocks with context-aware indices — header/footer Tab/indent mutates the wrong blocks or crashes
finding.evidence: This delta fixed the cursor-only path (`siblingsOf`, line 2869) to use `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` instead of `document.blocks`, but the multi-block-selection branch of the same walker three lines earlier still does `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks;` (line 2836) while `startIdx`/`endIdx` come from `this.doc.getBlockIndex()`, which is context-aware (`document.ts:271-273` → `getContextBlocks()`). With the caret in a header/footer (a state the delta explicitly declares supported and exercises via the new test) and a cross-block selection, indices resolved against `header.blocks` are used to index `document.blocks`: (a) if the body has fewer blocks than that index, `topLevel[i]` is `undefined` and `b.type` throws a TypeError inside handleTab/handleIndent (`fn(b, topLevel)` at 2849, and `handleIndent`'s own walk at 2754-2759 calls `block.style.marginLeft`), and (b) if the body is long enough, `applyListLevelChanges`/`applyBlockStyle` rewrite unrelated BODY blocks' listLevel/marginLeft while the selected header items are left untouched — a silent wrong-document mutation. The sibling implementation in `editor.ts` was written correctly (`const contextBlocks = doc.getContextBlocks();`, editor.ts:1689/1702), so the two walkers are now out of sync.

verdict.reason: The finding's central quoted evidence does not exist in the repository. It claims the multi-block-selection branch of forEachBlockInSelection does `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks;` at text-editor.ts:2836 and `fn(b, topLevel)` at 2849. In fact text-editor.ts:2843 reads `const contextBlocks = this.doc.getContextBlocks();`, line 2845 reads `const b = contextBlocks[i];`, and line 2856 reads `fn(b, contextBlocks);`. Lines 2836-2842 are a comment that explicitly explains that getContextBlocks() is used precisely because getBlockIndex is context-aware and indexing the body array would visit unrelated body blocks or undefined — i.e. the alleged bug is the documented rationale for the existing correct code. A file-wide grep for `topLevel` in text-editor.ts returns zero matches, so this is not line-number drift; the variable does not exist. The consequential claims fail with the premise: handleIndent (2750-2762) has no independent walk and reaches block.style.marginLeft at 2757 only via forEachBlockInSelection, and applyListLevelChanges (2712-2723) sources blocks solely from forEachBlockInSelection at 2714, both of which are context-aware on the multi-block branch (2843) and on the cursor-only fallback siblingsOf (2876). The 'out of sync with editor.ts' claim is also inverted: editor.ts:1689 uses `doc.getContextBlocks()`, matching text-editor.ts:2843. Neither the TypeError nor the wrong-block mutation can arise from this code.
